```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse   = TRUE,
  comment    = "#>",
  fig.width  = 7,
  fig.height = 4,
  dev        = "png",
  dpi        = 192
)
library(SeqPlotR)
library(GenomicRanges)
```

```{css echo = FALSE}
img { max-width: 100%; height: auto; }
```

Event-timing plots stack several views of one genome: structural-variant arches placed by event time, copy number with step ribbons, intervals around estimated times, and a two-channel heatmap of timing density. SeqPlotR provides generic elements for each view, and one adapter, `seq_rose_timing()`, that turns a table set written by ROSE into a plot built from those elements.

Every element draws what it is given. ROSE (or any other caller) supplies the positions, intervals, opacities, labels and colour categories, and SeqPlotR does no timing computation. Rows that carry a proxy bound are **order bounds, not times**: a bound says an event happened before or after a point, and the plots mark it as such.

The first half of this article uses toy data to show each element. The second half runs the adapter on the table sets shipped in `inst/extdata/rose/timing`.

```{r toy-common}
win <- GRanges("chr1", IRanges(1, 1e6))
page <- aes(margins = list(top = 0, right = 0.2, bottom = 0.02, left = 0))
```

# Count axis and paired ribbons

`seq_scale_count(max, log)` builds a copy-number axis with integer ticks. With `log = TRUE` it uses a pseudo-log transform (values up to 1 stay linear, larger values are placed at `1 + log2(v)`) and labels the ticks 0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16. Every element on the track, including `seq_point` and `seq_arch`, receives the transform, so values are given in count units.

`seq_paired_ribbon()` draws two thin ribbons per span: `y_up` upward and `y_down` downward.

```{r count-axis, fig.height = 3.2}
bands <- GRanges("chr1", IRanges(c(1, 4e5), c(4e5, 1e6)), major = c(2, 12), minor = c(1, 4))
snv <- GRanges("chr1", IRanges(c(1e5, 5e5, 8e5), width = 1), m = c(1.1, 11, 6))

seq_plot(aesthetics = page) %+%
  seq_track(
    track_id = "cn", windows = win,
    scale_y = seq_scale_count(12, log = TRUE),
    aesthetics = aes("axis.y.title.text" = "Copy number (log scale)"),
    elements = list(
      seq_paired_ribbon(bands, map(y_up = major, y_down = minor),
                        legend_labels = c(up = "Major CN", down = "Minor CN")),
      seq_point(snv, map(y = m))
    )
  ) -> p
p$plot()
```

# Step ribbons

`seq_step_ribbon()` draws a span at height `y` whose thickness scales with `thickness`. A vertical bar from `bar_lo` to `bar_hi` marks the interval, and a triangle of fixed size in millimetres points up or down whatever the span width. Labels are printed as given, so a label such as `+5` can sit on a ribbon of thickness 3.

```{r step-ribbon, fig.height = 3.2}
steps <- GRanges("chr1", IRanges(c(1, 3e5, 6e5), c(2.5e5, 5.5e5, 9e5)),
                 t = c(0.3, 0.55, 0.8), k = c(1, 2, 3), lab = c(NA, "+2", "+5"),
                 lo = c(0.2, 0.4, 0.6), hi = c(0.4, 0.7, 0.95),
                 dir = c("up", "down", "up"))

seq_plot(aesthetics = page) %+%
  seq_track(
    track_id = "steps", windows = win,
    scale_y = seq_scale_continuous(limits = c(0, 1)),
    aesthetics = aes("axis.y.title.text" = "Event time (tau)"),
    elements = list(
      seq_step_ribbon(steps, map(y = t, thickness = k, label = lab, bar_lo = lo,
                                 bar_hi = hi, pointing = dir),
                      legend_labels = c("1" = "1 copy", "2" = "2 copies", "3" = "3+ copies"))
    )
  ) -> p
p$plot()
```

# Interval glyphs

`seq_interval_glyph()` marks an anchor with one of five glyphs: `point` (a point with a bar), `latest` and `earliest` (a cap with an open bar, for one-sided bounds), `interval` (a bracket, with a point only when `y` is given) and `untimed` (nothing at the anchor). Rows with glyph `hidden` are dropped. `seq_glyph_legend_keys()` builds matching legend keys.

```{r glyphs, fig.height = 3.2}
g <- GRanges("chr1", IRanges(c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5) * 1.5e5, width = 1),
             y = c(0.5, 0.6, 0.4, NA, 0.3), lo = c(0.4, 0.2, 0.3, 0.1, 0.2),
             hi = c(0.6, 0.7, 0.8, 0.9, 0.5),
             kind = c("point", "latest", "earliest", "interval", "interval"),
             lab = c("A", NA, "+5", NA, NA))

seq_plot(aesthetics = page) %+%
  seq_track(
    track_id = "glyphs", windows = win,
    scale_y = seq_scale_continuous(limits = c(0, 1)),
    elements = list(
      seq_interval_glyph(g, map(y = y, bar_lo = lo, bar_hi = hi, glyph = kind, label = lab),
                         legend_all = TRUE)
    )
  ) -> p
p$plot()
```

# Cross-track arches

`seq_cross_arch()` is added to the track that holds the arch stems and names the track whose axis places the arch tops with `target`. The two tracks must have the same windows. The top is given in the target track's units, so an arch top lines up with a point or glyph drawn at the same value on the target track. Optional fields draw interval bars on both stems (`glyph`, `bar_lo`, `bar_hi`), a marker on each stem (`marker`) and a caution mark (`caution`). A row without `x1` becomes a single stem, and a row with no `top` reaches the top of the target axis. An anchor outside every window stops with a message that names the row.

```{r cross-arch, fig.height = 4.5}
arch <- data.frame(
  chr = "chr1", pos1 = c(1e5, 4e5, 7e5, 8.5e5), pos2 = c(3e5, 6e5, NA, 9.5e5),
  top = c(0.5, NA, 0.7, 0.35), g = c("point", "untimed", "latest", "interval"),
  lo = c(0.4, NA, 0.2, 0.25), hi = c(0.6, NA, NA, 0.45), m = c(2, 3, 1.5, 4),
  col = c("#E69F00", "grey70", "#009E73", "#7B3294"), ca = c(FALSE, FALSE, TRUE, FALSE)
)

seq_plot(aesthetics = page) %+%
  seq_track(track_id = "sv", windows = win, direction = "under",
            scale_y = seq_scale_continuous(limits = c(0, 1)),
            aesthetics = aes("axis.y.title.text" = "Event time (tau)")) %+%
  seq_track(
    track_id = "cn", windows = win, direction = "under",
    scale_y = seq_scale_continuous(limits = c(0, 4)),
    aesthetics = aes("axis.y.title.text" = "Multiplicity"),
    elements = list(
      seq_cross_arch(arch, map(chrom0 = chr, x0 = pos1, chrom1 = chr, x1 = pos2, top = top,
                               glyph = g, bar_lo = lo, bar_hi = hi, marker = m,
                               color = col, caution = ca),
                     target = "sv", aesthetics = aes(bar_alpha = 0.35, glyph_points = FALSE),
                     legend_extra = c(unname(seq_glyph_legend_keys(c("point", "latest", "interval", "untimed")))))
    )
  ) -> p
p$plot()
```

# Two-channel heatmap

`seq_tile_mix()` colours each tile by mixing two intensities in `[0, 1]`: the hue moves from `color_a` to `color_b` with the share of `b`, and the larger intensity sets the depth. Tiles with both intensities zero are not drawn. By default it adds a two-dimensional key from `seq_legend_2d()`; pass `legend = FALSE` to omit it. Bound lines compose from `seq_segment()`.

```{r tile-mix, fig.height = 3.5}
tiles <- GRanges("chr1", IRanges(seq(1, 9e5, by = 1e5), width = 1e5),
                 lo = rep(c(0.2, 0.4), length.out = 9), hi = rep(c(0.4, 0.6), length.out = 9),
                 a = c(0, 0.2, 0.5, 0.8, 0.6, 0.3, 0, 0.1, 0.4),
                 b = c(0, 0.1, 0.2, 0.5, 0.6, 0.9, 0.7, 0.4, 0))
bound <- GRanges("chr1", IRanges(4e5, 7e5), y = 0.6)

seq_plot(aesthetics = page) %+%
  seq_track(
    track_id = "heat", windows = win,
    scale_y = seq_scale_continuous(limits = c(0, 1)),
    aesthetics = aes("axis.y.title.text" = "Event time (tau)"),
    elements = list(
      seq_tile_mix(tiles, map(y_min = lo, y_max = hi, a = a, b = b),
                   aesthetics = aes(color_a = "#D62728", color_b = "#2B59C3"),
                   legend = seq_legend_2d("#D62728", "#2B59C3",
                                          x_title = "Channel a", y_title = "Channel b")),
      seq_segment(bound, map(x = start, x_end = end, y = y, y_end = y), aes(color = "#2B59C3"))
    )
  ) -> p
p$plot()
```

# Node-link panel

`seq_node_link()` draws nodes, edges and group boxes at the positions given. It runs no layout algorithm. Nodes can carry an interval bar and one of five shapes. Edges can carry an arrow, a label printed as given and a flag marking a conflict.

```{r node-link, fig.height = 3.5}
nodes <- data.frame(id = c("A", "B", "C"), x = c(1, 2, 3), y = c(0.2, 0.6, 0.4),
                    bar_lo = c(0.1, 0.5, NA), bar_hi = c(0.3, 0.7, NA),
                    shape = c("circle", "triangle_up", "diamond"),
                    fill = c("#7F7F7F", "#A50F15", "black"), label = c("a", "b", NA))
edges <- data.frame(from = c("A", "A", "B"), to = c("B", "B", "C"),
                    arrow = c(TRUE, FALSE, TRUE), label = c("fixed", ">0.99", NA),
                    flag = c(FALSE, TRUE, FALSE), linetype = c(1, 2, 1))
groups <- data.frame(x = 2, y = 0.9, label = "group 1")

seq_plot(aesthetics = page) %+%
  seq_track(
    track_id = "nodes", windows = GRanges("events", IRanges(1, 1)),
    scale_x = seq_scale_continuous(limits = c(0.4, 3.6)),
    scale_y = seq_scale_continuous(limits = c(-0.03, 1.03)),
    aesthetics = aes("axis.x.visible" = FALSE),
    elements = list(seq_node_link(nodes = nodes, edges = edges, groups = groups))
  ) -> p
p$plot()
```

# Span strips

`seq_span_strip()` labels spans with a coloured bar. With `bar_height = 0` only the labels are drawn.

```{r span-strip, fig.height = 1.8}
spans <- GRanges("chr1", IRanges(c(1e5, 5e5, 9e5), c(3e5, 7e5, 9.5e5)),
                 nm = c("a", "b", NA), col = c("tomato", NA, "steelblue"))

seq_plot(aesthetics = page) %+%
  seq_track(track_id = "bars", windows = win, scale_y = seq_scale_continuous(limits = c(0, 1)),
            elements = list(seq_span_strip(spans, map(label = nm, fill = col), aes(bar_y = 0.3)))) %+%
  seq_track(track_id = "text", windows = win, direction = "under",
            scale_y = seq_scale_continuous(limits = c(0, 1)),
            elements = list(seq_span_strip(spans, map(label = nm), aes(bar_height = 0)))) -> p
p$plot()
```

# Extending the elements

The base classes `SeqElementR6`, `SeqLinkR6`, `SeqArchR6` and `SeqPointR6` are exported so that new elements can subclass them without reaching into the package. `seq_to_canvas(x, y, panel)` maps a data position through a panel, applying the track's y transform, and is what `seq_cross_arch()` uses to place tops on another track. A link's `prep()` receives the panels of all tracks in `layout_all_tracks`, named by `track_id`.

# The ROSE adapter

ROSE writes a `plot_timing` table set: windows, copy-number bands, SNV points, SV arches, copy-number steps, glyphs, the heatmap and its bounds, poset nodes, edges and groups, annotations and settings. `seq_read_table_set()` reads it from a directory (or an in-memory list) and checks the schema version; an unsupported version or a missing column stops with a message that names the set, table and column.

```{r read-set}
tm <- system.file("extdata", "rose", "timing", package = "SeqPlotR")
list.files(tm)
tb <- seq_read_table_set(file.path(tm, "sim_bfb_amplicon"), "plot_timing")
names(tb)
attr(tb, "schema_version")
```

`seq_rose_timing(x, layout, poset_view, ...)` accepts a directory or a list and returns a `SeqPlot` built from the elements above. It only selects rows, renames columns and looks up colours in a palette; every position, interval, opacity and label comes from the tables.

| `layout` | Tracks |
|----------|--------|
| `"arches"` | SV event time with arches over copy number and step ribbons |
| `"order"` | arches placed at their poset layer |
| `"heatmap"` | arches over a two-channel timing heatmap |
| `"poset"` | node-link view (`poset_view` = `"poset"`, `"hasse"` or `"groups"`) |

Annotation and glyph labels get a strip above the genomic tracks, and an ideogram (or, with `plain = TRUE`, a genomic axis) closes the plot. The `palette` argument replaces any of the default colour sets by name, for example `palette = list(sv = c(DEL = "black"))`.

```{r adapter-opts, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(dpi = 600, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 6.5)
```

## An amplicon with five SVs

The arches layout shows each SV at its estimated event time on the top track. Bars are intervals reported by ROSE. The copy-number track shows the major and minor copy number, SNV multiplicities and the arch ends, and the bottom track shows copy-number gain and loss steps at their event times, with `+2` marking a two-copy step.

```{r bfb-arches}
bfb <- file.path(tm, "sim_bfb_amplicon")
p <- seq_rose_timing(bfb, layout = "arches")
p$plot()
```

The order layout places the same arches at their layer in the partial order instead of at a time (layer 0 is unordered).

```{r bfb-order}
p <- seq_rose_timing(bfb, layout = "order")
p$plot()
```

The heatmap layout replaces the step ribbons with the timing density of gains (red) and losses (blue).

```{r bfb-heatmap}
p <- seq_rose_timing(bfb, layout = "heatmap")
p$plot()
```

The poset layout draws the events of the partial order at their time estimates. An edge is labelled with the probability that the first event precedes the second, or `fixed` for an order given as a constraint.

```{r bfb-poset}
p <- seq_rose_timing(bfb, layout = "poset")
p$plot()
```

`poset_view = "hasse"` keeps only the reduction edges, and `"groups"` draws the groups of events that cannot be separated.

```{r bfb-hasse}
p <- seq_rose_timing(bfb, layout = "poset", poset_view = "hasse")
p$plot()
```

## Whole-genome doubling and losses

This fixture has three windows and no SV arches. Glyphs marked `earliest` and `latest` are proxy rows: they place an event before or after a point, so they are drawn as one-sided bounds rather than as times. SNVs above the axis maximum are excluded with a message.

```{r wgd-arches}
wgd <- file.path(tm, "sim_wgd_losses")
p <- seq_rose_timing(wgd, layout = "arches")
p$plot()
```

```{r wgd-heatmap}
p <- seq_rose_timing(wgd, layout = "heatmap")
p$plot()
```

```{r wgd-groups}
p <- seq_rose_timing(wgd, layout = "poset", poset_view = "groups")
p$plot()
```

## A single gain

```{r gain-arches}
gain <- file.path(tm, "sim_simple_gain")
p <- seq_rose_timing(gain, layout = "arches", plain = TRUE)
p$plot()
```

The returned plot can be extended like any other. Here an extra track with the same windows is added at the bottom.

```{r extend, fig.height = 7}
wg <- seq_read_table_set(gain, "plot_timing")$windows
wg <- GRanges(wg$chr, IRanges(wg$start, wg$end))
p <- seq_rose_timing(gain, layout = "arches") %+%
  seq_track(track_id = "extra", windows = wg, direction = "under", track_height = 0.4)
p$plot()
```

## What ROSE does not yet provide

The adapter uses only what the tables carry, and a few things are left to the caller or to a later ROSE export: genome-wide events such as WGD have no position in `glyphs` and so cannot be placed; there is no flag saying whether the heatmap holds SNV-derived density; the copy-number axis maximum is derived from the tables rather than stored; and annotation colours are assigned from `flexoki_palette()` because the tables name classes without a palette.
